title: 8 rules for Claude Code hooks that never get in Claude's way
content: My app runs one small Node script on every hook event Claude Code fires. Eleven events, every session, all day. If that script is slow, Claude is slow. If it crashes the wrong way, Claude stops. After a few weeks of that, these are the rules the script follows. None of them are clever. Each one is there because I broke it once. 1. Exit 0. Always. Claude Code reads your exit code. Exit 2 blocks the action and hands your stderr to Claude as feedback. Any other non-zero code shows up as a hook error. Neither is what you want when your JSON parse fails or your server is down. So the script has exactly one way out: const done = () => process . exit ( 0 ) Missing environment variable: done() . Broken JSON on stdin: done() . Connection refused: done() . The only time a hook should change what Claude does is when you decided it should. 2. title: Building MCP Servers in 2026: What Changed and What Production Needs
content: This is a condensed version of our full MCP Development Guide 2026 , which includes working TypeScript and Python servers, the full OAuth flow and a security checklist. If you learned the Model Context Protocol from a 2025 tutorial, parts of it no longer apply. The 2026-07-28 specification made MCP stateless, and that changes how you design, scale and secure a server. We build and run the hosted MCP server for Feedlio, our social media SaaS, which is listed on the official MCP Registry, Smithery and mcpservers.org. These are the points that mattered most in production. What changed in 2026-07-28 No initialize handshake. Every request carries its protocol version and client capabilities in _meta . Servers implement server/discover to advertise what they support. No protocol sessions. The Mcp-Session-Id header is gone. title: Using Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI on the same repository
content: Each coding agent has days when it's the right tool. Running all three on one repository is easy; keeping them consistent is the work. This is how to share instructions and tools between Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, keep their work apart, and hand tasks between them. One set of instructions, three readers Each agent looks for its own instructions file: Agent Reads by default Codex AGENTS.md Claude Code CLAUDE.md Gemini CLI GEMINI.md Keep the real content in one file, AGENTS.md , and point the others at it: Claude Code: CLAUDE.md can import another file with an @ line, so a one-line CLAUDE.md works: @AGENTS.md Gemini CLI: its settings can name the files it reads. In .gemini/settings.json : { "context" : { "fileName" : [ "AGENTS.md" , "GEMINI.md" ] } } Codex: reads AGENTS.md as it is.
author: Roi Dayan
summary_zh: 文章讲在同一仓库里同时使用 Claude Code、Codex 和 Gemini CLI 时，如何保持三者行为一致。核心做法是把指令只写在 AGENTS.md 一个文件里：CLAUDE.md 用一行 @AGENTS.md 导入，Gemini CLI 在 .gemini/settings.json 的 context.fileName 中加上 AGENTS.md，Codex 默认就读 AGENTS.md。文章还讲了共享工具、隔离各自的改动以及在代理之间交接任务的思路。

title: What Can Your Agent Actually Touch?
content: This article first appeared on Medium: https://medium.com/@r3dtuxedo/what-can-your-agent-actually-touch-6010c17243d9 Sandboxes, network access and MCP filesystem overreach. A bad web page can steer your agent, and nothing inside the model stops it. What limits the damage is the sandbox, the network rules and which secrets are in reach. Your MCP servers usually sit outside all three. TL;DR Nothing inside the model separates a web page's text from your instructions. Text the agent reads can steer what it does next. That's prompt injection, and the defence is outside the model: what runs without asking you, which files it can reach, where it can send data, and which secrets are in its environment. The defaults differ a lot. Codex sandboxes commands with network off. Cursor sandboxes them when it can. Claude Code's sandbox is off until you turn it on. OpenCode has no sandbox. title: Auto-format every file Claude Code edits with a PostToolUse hook
content: Claude Code writes decent code, but it doesn't always match your formatter. You can keep asking it to "run prettier", or you can make formatting automatic with a PostToolUse hook. What a PostToolUse hook does Hooks are shell commands Claude Code runs at fixed points. A PostToolUse hook runs right after a tool call finishes. Point it at the edit tools and your formatter runs every time a file changes. Add this to .claude/settings.json in your project: { "hooks" : { "PostToolUse" : [ { "matcher" : "Edit|MultiEdit|Write" , "hooks" : [ { "type" : "command" , "command" : "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path' | xargs -r npx prettier --write --ignore-unknown" } ] } ] }
author: Vildanden
summary_zh: 文章介绍如何用 Claude Code 的 PostToolUse hook 自动格式化文件：在 .claude/settings.json 中把 Edit、MultiEdit、Write 工具配置为匹配项，用 jq 取出被修改文件的路径，再交给 prettier 格式化。这样不用每次提醒 Claude 运行格式化工具，代码风格也能自动统一。配置简短，可以直接复制使用。

title: Claude Code Subagent allowed-tools: Syntax, Examples, Fixes
content: Originally published at Unattended . Claude Code subagents don't have an allowed-tools field. The key you want in a subagent's .md frontmatter is tools . It's an allowlist, written as a comma-separated string like tools: Read, Grep, Glob or as a YAML list. disallowedTools is the matching denylist. allowed-tools belongs to Skills, and it does something else: it pre-approves tools for one turn and restricts nothing. If you leave tools out, the subagent " Inherits every tool available to subagents if omitted. " Which option is right for you? The best place to start depends on whether you want a safe default fast, a dependable daily setup, or the lowest token cost. Your situation What to pick first First page to open Beginner, first custom subagent tools: Read, Grep, Glob (read-only). Nothing can break Create custom subagents Daily work, subagent edits code and runs tests tools: Read, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob plus a permissions.deny rule for risky Bash commands Configure permissions Subagent
author: Aoba Works
summary_zh: 文章澄清了一个常见误区：Claude Code 子代理的 .md frontmatter 里没有 allowed-tools 字段。限制工具应使用 tools（白名单，可写成逗号分隔字符串或 YAML 列表），对应的黑名单是 disallowedTools。allowed-tools 是 Skills 的字段，只在单轮中预先授权工具，并不起限制作用；不写 tools 时，子代理会继承全部可用工具。文章还按新手、日常使用、节省 token 等场景给出推荐配置，比如只读组合 Read, Grep, Glob。

title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
content: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts Parameter Labs describe an exploit they found against ChatGPT's implementation of the artifacts pattern (OpenAI used to call this "Canvas" but it looks like the latest revision is called HTML previews ), where interactive custom HTML apps are displayed in a sandboxed iframe. It's important that HTML in these stays tightly sandboxed to avoid untrusted code interacting with OpenAI APIs and accessing private data. Parameter found quite a complex attack chain. OpenAI use the MathLive JavaScript library as part of their graph support, and that library includes its own virtual keyboard , which can be triggered in the parent page via postMessage() from the sandboxed iframe. That message receiving code uses innerHTML , so anything that sends a message can add custom HTML to the parent - and there was no mechanism to prevent other sandboxed frames, including HTML preview frames, from calling that method. This meant untrusted code in an iframe could insert HTML,
summary_zh: Parameter Labs 披露了 ChatGPT 中 HTML 预览（原 Canvas/artifacts 模式）沙箱 iframe 的一条账户接管攻击链：沙箱 iframe 通过 postMessage() 唤起父页面中 MathLive 库的虚拟键盘，而父页面接收消息的代码使用 innerHTML，导致可注入任意内容并越出沙箱。这个案例说明，构建 LLM 应用中运行不可信生成代码的 artifacts 类功能时，第三方库和跨 frame 通信的安全隔离至关重要。

title: Claude Code blocks recreation of existing games
content: 📅 2 November 2026 • TNW / PC Gamer A server-side update to Claude Code, first noticed around 27 October, blocks the tool from recreating specific existing games. The restriction applies even when the game is renamed or called original — the model declines requests aimed at a named, commercially released game rather than treating the task as a genre exercise. Because the change is delivered server-side, it took effect without a client update and without an entry in the official changelog. The boundary leaves most creative use untouched. Original games built from scratch, genre games in established categories such as platformers, roguelikes or puzzle games, and projects using the user's own designs and assets all continue to work. In practice the line runs between building a game in a genre and building a copy of a particular title. Anthropic has confirmed the policy. title: Claude Ultra 요금제: 월 200달러로 지금 누리는 혜택
content: Claude Ultra 요금제: 월 200달러로 지금 누리는 혜택 Claude Ultra 플랜은 Max 20x의 새 이름입니다. 2026년 10월 30일, Anthropic은 Max 5x를 Claude Max(월 $100)로, Max 20x를 Claude Ultra(월 $200)로 이름을 변경했습니다. 인증된 Ultra 계정에서는 5시간 사용량 윈도우가 사라지고, Pro의 10배에 해당하는 주간 한도는 유지되며, 매월 $200의 Claude API 크레딧을 받습니다. 지금 Apidog를 사용해 보세요 가격 변동은 없었고, 기존 Max 20x 구독자는 자동으로 전환되었습니다. 이 글에서는 바뀐 한도, 계정 인증, API 크레딧, 그리고 Max와 Ultra 중 무엇을 선택할지 다룹니다. Claude Ultra 플랜이란 무엇인가요? Claude Ultra는 Anthropic의 최상위 개인 구독 상품으로, 웹 기준 월 $200입니다. 동일한 가격으로 Max 20x를 대체하며 다음을 제공합니다: Pro 플랜의 10배에 달하는 주간 사용량 계정 인증 후에는 5시간 제한 없음 동일 구독에 포함된 Claude Code 신규 모델 및 기능 조기 액세스 매월 $200의 Claude API 크레딧 Ultra 도움말 문서 에 이 혜택들이 나열되어 있고, 결제 전에 알아두면 좋은 세부 사항이 추가로 안내되어 있습니다: Ultra는 월간 결제만 가능합니다. 연간 Ultra 플랜은 없습니다. 모바일 앱 가격은 웹 가격($200)과 다를 수 있습니다. 주간 한도는 모든 모델에 적용되며, Fable에는 별도의 주간 한도가 있습니다. Anthropic은 재량에 따라 추가 한도를 적용할 수 있다고 밝히고 있습니다. Max 20x를 써 봤다면, Ultra는 계량기만 바뀐 동일한 좌석이라고 이해하면 됩니다. title: webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox
content: Research: webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox webframe is a neat little project from Jeff Lindsay which lets you "run a web page like a program" - you point it at a URL or file and it executes it in a hidden headless web view and outputs console.log() to standard output and any exceptions to standard error. It's written in Go on top of the glaze library, which provides access to a system browser ("WKWebView on macOS, WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows") so it doesn't need to bundle its own browser engine. It reminds me of my own shot-scraper javascript tool, albeit in a much smaller package that doesn't depend on Playwright. I had Claude Opus 5.5 put it through its paces and prepare a research report for me. Here's the prompt I used: Explore https://github.com/tractordev/webframe try running it and put it though its paces, build a few exploratory prototypes, then evaluate it as a potential sandboxing tool and as a tool for scraping web pages using the same patterns enco
summary_zh: Simon Willison 让 Claude Opus 5.5 评估 Jeff Lindsay 的 webframe 项目，并写出研究报告。webframe 用 Go 写成，基于 glaze 库调用系统自带的 WebView，可以把网页当作命令行程序在无头环境里运行，把 console.log 输出到标准输出、异常输出到标准错误。文章从爬虫和沙箱两个角度评估它，并公开了所用的提示词，可作为让 AI 智能体做开源项目技术调研的参考案例。

Reject numeric prefixes, fractions and unsafe window integers consistently with summary scheduling while preserving resolver precedence. title: Why an AI Agent Should Never Be Its Own Security Guard
content: Imagine giving an employee the keys to your company database, asking them to make important business decisions, and then telling them to check with themselves before doing anything dangerous. Sounds ridiculous, right? Yet this is surprisingly close to how some AI agent systems are designed. The same model that interprets a request, decides which tools to use, and generates the arguments for a database operation is sometimes also expected to decide whether that operation is safe. That creates a problem. Not because AI models are useless, but because the system making a decision should not be the only thing responsible for enforcing the rules around that decision. If we're serious about building AI agents that can operate real business systems, we need to separate intelligence from authority. And that distinction matters more than most people realize. title: Quoting Ted Sanders
content: In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered: Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra [ ... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it's not 5.7), and isn't a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7. — Ted Sanders , explaining OpenAI's model naming conventions T
summary_zh: 这篇文章引用了 Ted Sanders 的一段话。他认为大模型的能力是多维度的，擅长数学的模型不一定也擅长讲笑话，但性能差异大多可以用模型规模来解释：模型越大，可靠性越高、每 token 成本越高，对冷门知识的记忆也越好。他还介绍了 Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra 的模型档位排序，以及版本号同时代表的三层含义：发布先后、与其他版本的关系、提升幅度。这些内容有助于理解模型命名和怎样按任务选择模型规模，但对编程实践的直接帮助有限。
